blocks.text: A precious teaching is called מרגנותא (Berachoth 33b).

Finally, we include here the insect תולעת שני, “shining worm.” Crimson-dyed wool is called שני תולעת, which Maimuni (on Negaim [p. 349] 14, 1) explains as: צמר צבוע בכרמיז, “wool dyed in crimson.” Crimson is prepared from the swollen egg sacs of a kind of tortoise. These eggs are found on the leaves of the holly. The eggs resemble small seedless raisins and dye a brownish red. Rashi (on Jes. 1, 18) says: In the eggs lie worms (חולעים), which yield the red colour. The eggs, however, are also called dye grain or dye berry, which is why I place this article here among the zoophytes; cf. Rosenmüller (loc. cit. 4, 2. p. 447 ff.).

Besides our species of tortoise, the juice of the trumpet shell (p. 281), of the purple snail (p. 282), of the cuttlefish (p. 283), and the blood of cattle (§. 102) were also used for dyeing. On the dyeing of the antelope's horn see B. batra 16b and Rashi there.

The Aramaic paraphrases take both שני חולעת (Exod. 25, 4) and שני חולעת (Num. 19, 6) only as a colour, namely as purple. It is interesting that Jonathan points the word שני only in the latter passage and the LXX only in the former.
On the oyster, which attaches itself to rocks, see above p. 285, note.
